title_en: Circular Economy Promotion Law of the People's Republic of China

articles.content_en: Article 1 This Law is enacted for the purpose of promoting the development of a circular economy, improving the efficiency of resource utilization, protecting and improving the environment, and achieving sustainable development.

Article 2 For the purposes of this Law, "circular economy" means the general term for activities of reduction, reuse and recycling conducted in the processes of production, circulation and consumption.
For the purposes of this Law, "reduction" means reducing resource consumption and waste generation in the processes of production, circulation and consumption.
For the purposes of this Law, "reuse" means using waste directly as products or continuing to use waste as products after repair, refurbishment or remanufacture, or using all or part of waste as components of other products.
For the purposes of this Law, "recycling" means using waste directly as raw materials or regenerating waste.

Article 3 Developing a circular economy is a major strategy for the national economic and social development. The principles of unified planning, rational distribution, adapting measures to local conditions, focusing on practical results, government promotion, market guidance, enterprise implementation and public participation shall be followed.

Article 4 The development of a circular economy shall be implemented under the premise of technical feasibility, economic rationality and being conducive to resource conservation and environmental protection, following the principle of giving priority to reduction.
In the process of waste reuse and recycling, production safety shall be ensured, product quality shall be guaranteed to meet the standards prescribed by the State, and secondary pollution shall be prevented.

Article 5 The comprehensive department of the State Council for the development of a circular economy shall be responsible for organizing, coordinating, supervising and administering the national circular economy development work; the competent departments for ecological environment and other relevant departments under the State Council shall be responsible for the supervision and administration of the circular economy within their respective functions.
The comprehensive departments of the local people's governments at or above the county level for the development of a circular economy shall be responsible for organizing, coordinating, supervising and administering the circular economy development work within their respective administrative regions; the competent departments for ecological environment and other relevant departments of the local people's governments at or above the county level shall be responsible for the supervision and administration of the circular economy within their respective functions.

Article 6 The industrial policies formulated by the State shall comply with the requirements for developing a circular economy.
When the local people's governments at or above the county level draw up national economic and social development plans and annual plans, and when the relevant departments of the local people's governments at or above the county level draw up plans for environmental protection, science and technology, etc., such plans shall include the content of developing a circular economy.

Article 7 The State encourages and supports the research, development and promotion of science and technology for the circular economy, and encourages the publicity, education, popularization of scientific knowledge and international cooperation in the circular economy.

Article 8 The local people's governments at or above the county level shall establish a target responsibility system for developing a circular economy, and adopt measures such as planning, finance, investment and government procurement to promote the development of a circular economy.

Article 9 Enterprises and public institutions shall establish and improve management systems, take measures to reduce resource consumption, reduce the amount of waste generated and discharged, and raise the level of waste reuse and recycling.

Article 10 Citizens shall enhance their awareness of resource conservation and environmental protection, consume rationally and save resources.
The State encourages and guides citizens to use energy-saving, water-saving, material-saving and environmentally friendly products and recycled products, and to reduce the amount of waste generated and discharged.
Citizens shall have the right to report acts of wasting resources and damaging the environment, and have the right to learn about the information of the government's development of a circular economy and to put forward opinions and suggestions.

Article 11 The State encourages and supports trade associations to play a role of technical guidance and service in the development of a circular economy. The local people's governments at or above the county level may entrust qualified trade associations and other social organizations to provide public services for promoting the development of a circular economy.
The State encourages and supports intermediary agencies, academic societies and other social organizations to carry out circular economy publicity, technology promotion and consulting services to promote the development of a circular economy.

Article 12 The comprehensive department of the State Council for the development of a circular economy shall, together with the competent departments for ecological environment and other relevant departments under the State Council, formulate a national circular economy development plan, which shall be submitted to the State Council for approval before being promulgated and implemented. The comprehensive departments of the local people's governments at or above the level of a city divided into districts for the development of a circular economy shall, together with the competent departments for ecological environment and other relevant departments of the people's government at the same level, formulate a circular economy development plan for their respective administrative regions, which shall be submitted to the people's government at the same level for approval before being promulgated and implemented.
A circular economy development plan shall include planning objectives, scope of application, main contents, key tasks and safeguard measures, and shall prescribe indicators such as resource productivity, waste reuse and recycling rates.

Article 13 The local people's governments at or above the county level shall, in accordance with the control targets for the total discharge of major pollutants, the total use of land for construction and the total water consumption issued by the people's government at a higher level for their respective administrative regions, plan and adjust the industrial structure in their administrative regions to promote the development of a circular economy.
New construction, reconstruction and expansion projects must meet the requirements of the control targets for the total discharge of major pollutants, the total use of land for construction and the total water consumption in the relevant administrative regions.

Article 14 The comprehensive department of the State Council for the development of a circular economy shall, together with the competent departments for statistics, ecological environment and other relevant departments under the State Council, establish and improve the circular economy evaluation indicator system.
The people's government at a higher level shall, according to the main evaluation indicators for the circular economy as prescribed in the preceding paragraph, regularly assess the status of the development of a circular economy by the people's government at a lower level, and shall take the completion status of the main evaluation indicators as part of the assessment and evaluation of the local people's government and its persons in charge.

Article 15 Where products or packaging materials are included in the list of products and packaging materials subject to compulsory recovery, the enterprises that produce such products or packaging materials must be responsible for recovering the discarded products or packaging materials; those that can be utilized shall be utilized by the respective production enterprises; and those that are not suitable for utilization due to lack of technical and economic conditions shall be disposed of harmlessly by the respective production enterprises.
Where a producer entrusts a seller or other organization to recover, or entrusts a waste utilization or disposal enterprise to utilize or dispose of, the discarded products or packaging materials specified in the preceding paragraph, the entrusted party shall be responsible for recovery, utilization or disposal in accordance with the provisions of relevant laws and administrative regulations and the contract.
For products and packaging materials included in the list of compulsory recovery, consumers shall deliver the discarded products or packaging materials to the producers or the sellers or other organizations entrusted by the producers for recovery.
The list of products and packaging materials subject to compulsory recovery and the measures for their administration shall be prescribed by the comprehensive department of the State Council for the development of a circular economy.

Article 16 The State shall implement a key supervision and administration system for energy consumption and water consumption for key enterprises in such industries as iron and steel, non-ferrous metals, coal, electric power, petroleum processing, chemical industry, building materials, construction, papermaking and printing and dyeing, whose annual comprehensive energy consumption and water consumption exceed the total amounts prescribed by the State.
The energy conservation supervision and administration for key energy-consuming entities shall be carried out in accordance with the provisions of the Energy Conservation Law of the People's Republic of China.
The supervision and administration measures for key water-using entities shall be prescribed by the comprehensive department of the State Council for the development of a circular economy together with the relevant departments under the State Council.

Article 17 The State shall establish and improve the circular economy statistical system, strengthen the statistical management of resource consumption, comprehensive utilization and waste generation, and regularly publish the main statistical indicators to the public.
The competent department of standardization under the State Council shall, together with the comprehensive department for the development of a circular economy under the State Council and the competent departments for ecological environment and other relevant departments, establish and improve the circular economy standard system, and formulate and perfect standards for energy conservation, water conservation, material conservation, waste reuse and recycling, etc.
The State shall establish and improve the product resource consumption labeling system, such as the energy efficiency labeling system.

Article 18 The comprehensive department of the State Council for the development of a circular economy shall, together with the competent departments for ecological environment and other relevant departments under the State Council, regularly publish a list of technologies, processes, equipment, materials and products that are encouraged, restricted or eliminated.
The production, import and sale of equipment, materials and products included in the list for elimination shall be prohibited, and the use of technologies, processes, equipment and materials included in the list for elimination shall be prohibited.

Article 19 The design of processes, equipment, products and packaging materials shall, in accordance with the requirements of reducing resource consumption and waste generation, give priority to the selection of materials and design schemes that are easy to recover, disassemble, degrade, non-toxic and harmless, or of low toxicity and low harm, and shall comply with the mandatory requirements of relevant national standards.
For electrical and electronic products that may cause environmental pollution during disassembly and disposal, no toxic and hazardous substances prohibited by the State shall be designed to be used. The list of toxic and hazardous substances prohibited from being used in electrical and electronic products shall be formulated by the comprehensive department of the State Council for the development of a circular economy together with the competent departments for ecological environment and other relevant departments under the State Council.
The packaging of products shall be designed in accordance with product packaging standards to prevent excessive packaging from causing resource waste and environmental pollution.

Article 20 Industrial enterprises shall adopt advanced or applicable water-saving technologies, processes and equipment, formulate and implement water-saving plans, strengthen water-saving management, and exercise control over the whole process of production water use.
Industrial enterprises shall strengthen the management of water metering, equip and use qualified water metering instruments, and establish a system for water consumption statistics and water use status analysis.
New construction, reconstruction and expansion projects shall include water-saving facilities. Water-saving facilities shall be designed, constructed and put into operation simultaneously with the main project.
The State encourages and supports the desalination of seawater and the direct use of seawater in coastal areas to save fresh water resources.

Article 21 The State encourages and supports enterprises to use highly efficient oil-saving products.
Enterprises in electric power, petroleum processing, chemical industry, iron and steel, non-ferrous metals and building materials must, within the scope and time limit prescribed by the State, replace fuel oil with clean energy such as clean coal, petroleum coke and natural gas, and cease to use fuel generator sets and fuel boilers that do not conform to the provisions of the State.
Manufacturing enterprises of internal combustion engines and motor vehicles shall, in accordance with the fuel economy standards for internal combustion engines and motor vehicles prescribed by the State, adopt oil-saving technologies to reduce the consumption of petroleum products.

Article 22 The exploitation of mineral resources shall be subject to unified planning, a rational development and utilization plan shall be formulated, and reasonable mining sequences, methods and beneficiation processes shall be adopted. The authority issuing the mining license shall, in accordance with the law, examine the indicators such as the mining recovery rate, mining dilution rate, beneficiation recovery rate, mine water recycling rate and land reclamation rate in the development and utilization plan submitted by the applicant; if the examination is not up to standard, the mining license shall not be issued. The authority issuing the mining license shall, in accordance with the law, strengthen the supervision and administration of the exploitation of mineral resources.
While mining the main mineral species, mining enterprises shall carry out comprehensive mining and rational utilization of associated and accompanying minerals of industrial value; for minerals that must be extracted simultaneously but cannot be utilized temporarily and for tailings containing useful components, protective measures shall be taken to prevent resource loss and ecological damage.

Article 23 Units engaged in architectural design, construction and building shall, in accordance with the relevant provisions and standards of the State, adopt technologies and processes for energy conservation, water conservation, land conservation and material conservation, as well as small-sized, light-duty and recycled products, for the buildings and structures designed, constructed and built by them. In regions where conditions permit, renewable energy sources such as solar energy, geothermal energy and wind energy shall be fully utilized.
The State encourages the use of non-toxic and harmless solid waste to produce building materials, encourages the use of bulk cement, and promotes the use of ready-mixed concrete and ready-mixed mortar.
The burning of bricks by destroying cultivated land shall be prohibited. Within the time limit and areas prescribed by the State Council or the people's governments of provinces, autonomous regions and municipalities directly under the Central Government, the production, sale and use of clay bricks shall be prohibited.

Article 24 The local people's governments at or above the county level and their competent departments for agriculture, etc., shall promote the intensive use of land, encourage and support agricultural producers to adopt advanced planting, breeding and irrigation technologies that save water, fertilizer and pesticides, promote energy conservation in agricultural machinery, and give priority to the development of ecological agriculture.
In water-deficient areas, the cropping structure shall be adjusted, priority shall be given to developing water-saving agriculture, the collection and utilization of rainwater shall be promoted, water-saving irrigation facilities shall be constructed and maintained, water use efficiency shall be raised, and water evaporation and leakage shall be reduced.

Article 25 State organs and other organizations using fiscal funds shall practice strict economy and eliminate waste, take the lead in using products, equipment and facilities that save energy, water, land and materials and are conducive to environmental protection, and use office supplies sparingly. The institutions of the State Council and the local people's governments at or above the county level in charge of government offices affairs shall, together with the relevant departments of the people's government at the same level, formulate the quota indicators for energy and water use for the State organs and other organizations at the same level, and the financial departments shall formulate expenditure standards based on such quota indicators.
The city people's governments and the owners or users of buildings shall take measures to strengthen the maintenance and management of buildings and extend the service life of buildings. For buildings that conform to the urban planning and construction standards and are within their reasonable service life, the city people's governments shall not decide to demolish them except for the needs of the public interest.

Article 26 Service enterprises such as those in catering, entertainment and hotel industries shall adopt products that save energy, water and materials and are conducive to environmental protection, and reduce or refrain from using products that waste resources and pollute the environment.
Service enterprises such as those in catering, entertainment and hotel industries newly built after the coming into force of this Law shall adopt technologies, equipment and facilities that save energy, water and materials and are conducive to environmental protection.

Article 27 The State encourages and supports the use of reclaimed water. In areas where reclaimed water is available, the use of tap water for urban road cleaning, urban greening and landscape water shall be restricted or prohibited.

Article 28 The State shall, on the premise of ensuring product safety and hygiene, restrict the production and sale of disposable consumer goods. The specific list shall be formulated by the comprehensive department of the State Council for the development of a circular economy together with the competent departments for finance, ecological environment and other relevant departments under the State Council.
For the production and sale of disposable consumer goods included in the list specified in the preceding paragraph, the competent departments for finance, taxation and foreign trade under the State Council shall formulate restrictive measures such as taxation and export.

Article 29 The local people's governments at or above the county level shall make unified planning for the regional economic layout, rationally adjust the industrial structure, and promote cooperation among enterprises in such fields as comprehensive utilization of resources, so as to achieve efficient utilization and recycling of resources.
All types of industrial parks shall organize enterprises within the parks to carry out comprehensive utilization of resources and promote the development of a circular economy.
The State encourages enterprises in all types of industrial parks to exchange and utilize waste, cascade energy, use land intensively, classify and recycle water, and share infrastructure and other relevant facilities.
Newly built and renovated industrial parks of all types shall, in accordance with the law, conduct environmental impact assessments and adopt ecological protection and pollution control measures to ensure that the environmental quality of the region meets the prescribed standards.

Article 30 Enterprises shall, in accordance with the provisions of the State, comprehensively utilize industrial wastes such as fly ash, coal gangue, tailings, waste rock, waste materials and waste gas generated in the production process.

Article 31 Enterprises shall develop cascade water use systems and circulating water use systems to increase the rate of water reuse.
Enterprises shall adopt advanced technologies, processes and equipment to regenerate and utilize the waste water generated in the production process.

Article 32 Enterprises shall adopt advanced or applicable recovery technologies, processes and equipment to comprehensively utilize the waste heat and waste pressure generated in the production process.
The construction of grid-connected power generation projects utilizing waste heat, waste pressure, coalbed methane, as well as low-calorific value fuels such as coal gangue, coal slime and garbage shall, in accordance with the laws and the provisions of the State Council, obtain an administrative license or be filed for record. Grid enterprises shall, in accordance with the provisions of the State, sign grid connection agreements with enterprises that generate electricity by comprehensively utilizing resources, provide grid access services, and purchase in full the on-grid electricity generated by the grid-connected power generation projects.

Article 33 Construction entities shall comprehensively utilize the construction waste generated during the construction of the project; if they do not have the conditions for comprehensive utilization, they shall entrust a production and operation entity that meets the conditions to carry out comprehensive utilization or harmless disposal.

Article 34 The State encourages and supports agricultural producers and related enterprises to adopt advanced or applicable technologies to comprehensively utilize crop straw, livestock and poultry manure, by-products of agricultural product processing, waste agricultural film, etc., and to develop and utilize biomass energy such as biogas.

Article 35 The local people's governments at or above the county level and their competent departments for forestry and grassland shall actively develop ecological forestry, encourage and support forestry producers and related enterprises to adopt wood-saving and substitution technologies, and carry out comprehensive utilization of forestry wastes, inferior fuelwood, sand shrubs, etc., so as to increase the comprehensive utilization rate of timber.

Article 36 The State supports producers and business operators in establishing an industrial waste exchange information system to promote the exchange of industrial waste information among enterprises.
Enterprises that do not have the conditions for comprehensive utilization of the waste generated in the production process shall provide such waste to producers and business operators that meet the conditions for comprehensive utilization.

Article 37 The State encourages and promotes the establishment of a waste recovery system.
Local people's governments shall, in accordance with urban and rural planning, rationally distribute waste recovery outlets and trading markets, and support waste recovery enterprises and other organizations in collecting, storing, transporting and exchanging information on waste.
Waste recovery trading markets shall comply with the provisions of the State on environmental protection, safety and fire protection.

Article 38 The disassembly or reuse of specific products such as waste electrical and electronic products, end-of-life motor vehicles and vessels, waste tires, waste lead-acid batteries, etc., shall comply with the provisions of relevant laws and administrative regulations.

Article 39 Recycled electrical and electronic products that are sold after repair must meet the standards for reused products and shall be marked as reused products in a conspicuous position.
Recycled electrical and electronic products that need to be disassembled and recycled shall be sold to disassembly enterprises that meet the conditions.

Article 40 The State supports enterprises in carrying out remanufacturing of products such as motor vehicle parts, construction machinery and machine tools, and the retreading of tires.
The quality of remanufactured products and retreaded products for sale must meet the standards prescribed by the State, and they shall be marked as remanufactured products or retreaded products in conspicuous positions.

Article 41 Local people's governments at or above the county level shall make unified plans for the construction of facilities for classified collection and recycling of urban and rural household waste, establish and improve a system for classified collection and recycling, and increase the recycling rate of household waste.
Local people's governments at or above the county level shall support enterprises in constructing facilities for recycling and disposing of sludge, raise the level of comprehensive utilization of sludge, and prevent secondary pollution.

Article 42 The State Council and the people's governments of provinces, autonomous regions and municipalities directly under the Central Government shall set up special funds for the development of a circular economy to support scientific and technological research and development, demonstration and promotion of circular economy technologies and products, implementation of major circular economy projects, and information services for the development of a circular economy. The specific measures shall be formulated by the competent department of finance under the State Council together with the comprehensive department for the development of a circular economy under the State Council and other relevant departments.

Article 43 The State Council, the people's governments of provinces, autonomous regions and municipalities directly under the Central Government, and their relevant departments shall include independent innovation research, application demonstration and industrial development of major circular economy key scientific and technological projects in the national or provincial science and technology development plans and high-tech industry development plans, and shall arrange fiscal funds to support them.
Where major circular economy technologies and equipment are introduced with fiscal funds, plans for digestion, absorption and innovation shall be formulated, submitted to the relevant competent department for approval, and implemented under its supervision; the relevant competent department shall, according to actual needs, establish a coordination mechanism, exercise overall coordination over the introduction, digestion, absorption and innovation of major technologies and equipment, and provide financial support.

Article 44 The State grants tax preferences for industrial activities that promote the development of a circular economy, and adopts tax and other measures to encourage the import of advanced energy-saving, water-saving and material-saving technologies, equipment and products, and to restrict the export of products with high energy consumption and heavy pollution in the production process. The specific measures shall be formulated by the competent departments of finance and taxation under the State Council.
Enterprises that use or produce technologies, processes, equipment or products included in the national encouraged list for clean production, comprehensive utilization of resources, etc., shall enjoy tax preferences in accordance with the relevant provisions of the State.

Article 45 When formulating and implementing investment plans, the comprehensive departments of the local people's governments at or above the county level for the development of a circular economy shall list projects for energy conservation, water conservation, land conservation, material conservation and comprehensive utilization of resources as key investment areas.
For projects that comply with the national industrial policies on energy conservation, water conservation, land conservation, material conservation and comprehensive utilization of resources, financial institutions shall give priority to credit support such as loans and actively provide supporting financial services.
For enterprises that produce, import, sell or use technologies, processes, equipment, materials or products included in the list for elimination, financial institutions shall not provide any form of credit support.

Article 46 The State implements pricing policies conducive to resource conservation and rational utilization, guiding entities and individuals to conserve and rationally use resource products such as water, electricity and gas.
The competent pricing departments of the State Council and of the people's governments of provinces, autonomous regions and municipalities directly under the Central Government shall, in accordance with the national industrial policies, implement restrictive pricing policies for restricted projects in industries with high resource consumption.
For grid-connected power generation projects utilizing waste heat, waste pressure, coalbed methane, and low-calorific value fuels such as coal gangue, coal slime and garbage, the competent pricing departments shall determine the on-grid electricity prices in accordance with the principle of being conducive to the comprehensive utilization of resources.
The people's governments of provinces, autonomous regions and municipalities directly under the Central Government may, based on the economic and social development status of their respective administrative regions, implement a garbage discharge charging system. The fees collected shall be used exclusively for garbage classification, collection, transportation, storage, utilization and disposal, and shall not be misappropriated for other purposes.
The State encourages the recovery of waste through methods such as trade-in and deposit.

Article 47 The State implements government procurement policies conducive to the development of a circular economy. Where procurement is made with fiscal funds, priority shall be given to the procurement of products that save energy, water and materials and are conducive to environmental protection, as well as recycled products.

Article 48 Local people's governments at or above the county level and their relevant departments shall give commendations and awards to entities and individuals that have made remarkable achievements in circular economy management, scientific and technological research, product development, demonstration and promotion.
Enterprises and public institutions shall give commendations and awards to collectives and individuals that have made outstanding contributions to the development of a circular economy.

Article 49 Where the comprehensive department of a local people's government at or above the county level for the development of a circular economy or any other relevant competent department fails to investigate and deal with a violation of this Law after discovering it or after receiving a report on such a violation, or commits any other act of failing to perform its supervision and administration functions according to law, the people's government at the same level or the relevant competent department of the people's government at the next higher level shall order it to make corrections, and the persons directly in charge and other persons directly responsible shall be given sanctions according to law.

Article 50 Whoever produces or sells products or equipment included in the list for elimination shall be punished in accordance with the provisions of the Product Quality Law of the People's Republic of China.
Whoever uses technologies, processes, equipment or materials included in the list for elimination shall be ordered by the comprehensive department of the local people's government at or above the county level for the development of a circular economy to cease the use, the illegally used equipment and materials shall be confiscated, and a fine of not less than 50,000 yuan but not more than 200,000 yuan shall be imposed; if the circumstances are serious, the comprehensive department for the development of a circular economy shall submit its opinions to the people's government at the same level, which shall, in accordance with the authority prescribed by the State Council, order the suspension of business or closure.
Whoever, in violation of the provisions of this Law, imports equipment, materials or products included in the list for elimination shall be ordered by the Customs to return them, and a fine of not less than 100,000 yuan but not more than 1,000,000 yuan may be imposed. If the importer is unknown, the carrier shall bear the responsibility for return or bear the relevant disposal costs.

Article 51 Where any entity, in violation of this Law, designs and uses toxic and hazardous substances included in the national catalogue of prohibited substances for use in electrical and electronic products that may cause environmental pollution during the dismantling or disposal process, the market regulation department of the local people's government at or above the county level shall order it to make corrections within a prescribed period; if it fails to make corrections within the prescribed period, it shall be fined not less than 20,000 yuan but not more than 200,000 yuan; if the circumstances are serious, its business license shall be revoked according to law.

Article 52 Where any entity, in violation of this Law, such as an enterprise in the electric power, petroleum processing, chemical, iron and steel, non-ferrous metal, or building materials industry, fails to stop using fuel oil generator sets or fuel oil boilers that do not meet the national provisions within the prescribed scope or time limit, the comprehensive department in charge of circular economy development of the local people's government at or above the county level shall order it to make corrections within a prescribed period; if it fails to make corrections within the prescribed period, it shall be ordered to dismantle the fuel oil generator sets or fuel oil boilers and shall be fined not less than 50,000 yuan but not more than 500,000 yuan.

Article 53 Where a mining enterprise, in violation of this Law, fails to meet the indicators such as the mining recovery rate, mining dilution rate, ore dressing recovery rate, mine water recycling rate, and land reclamation rate as determined after examination according to law, the geological and mineral resources department of the local people's government at or above the county level shall order it to make corrections within a prescribed period and impose a fine of not less than 50,000 yuan but not more than 500,000 yuan; if it fails to make corrections within the prescribed period, the organ issuing the mining license shall revoke the mining license according to law.

Article 54 Where any entity, in violation of this Law, produces, sells, or uses clay bricks within the period or region where the State Council or the people's government of a province, autonomous region, or municipality directly under the Central Government has prohibited the production, sale, or use of clay bricks, the department designated by the local people's government at or above the county level shall order it to make corrections within a prescribed period; if there are illegal gains, the illegal gains shall be confiscated; if it continues to produce or sell after the prescribed period, the market regulation department of the local people's government shall revoke its business license according to law.

Article 55 Where a power grid enterprise, in violation of this Law, refuses to purchase electricity generated by enterprises using waste heat, waste pressure, coalbed methane, and low calorific value fuels such as coal gangue, coal slime, and garbage, the state electricity regulatory authority shall order it to make corrections within a prescribed period; if it causes losses to the enterprise, it shall bear compensation liability according to law.
Article 57 Where any entity, in violation of this Law, commits an act constituting a crime, criminal liability shall be investigated according to law.
Article 58 This Law shall come into force as of January 1, 2009.
